subject: ventures/grazing-lease-rate-calculator
professional: a ranch-management extension specialist (or agricultural appraiser) who prices pasture leases; first checks: is the AUM the NRCS 1,000 lb animal unit at about 26 lb dry matter a day, is utilisation treated as harvest efficiency (NRCS/UNL about 25% under continuous grazing), is a cow-calf pair priced per month as the AUM rate times its animal-unit equivalent, is the hay substitute converted to dry matter with waste, and does the owner floor compare like with like

evidence.correctness: Recomputed the sample (640 ac, 1,800 lb/ac, 35% use, 180 days, 1.2 AU/head, $24/AUM, $14 alt, $3 owner cost, $190 hay at 86% DM and 15% waste, $3 extra) by hand in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/01267756-bf5d-5ffa-b429-738a5f63cbd7/scratchpad/gl/re.mjs from the NRCS National Range and Pasture Handbook AUM definition (1,000 lb AU, 26 lb DM/day) and the standard hay-as-substitute build-up: usable 403,200 lb, AUMs 510.12 (26 x 30.4 lb), AU 86.15, head 71.79, hay 790.4/0.86/0.85/2000 x 190 = $102.72, ceiling $99.72, owner floor 17/0.797 = $21.33, annual rent $12,242.91: all match (with NRCS's 780 lb/30-day AUM the count is 516.92, a 1.3% convention difference). One shipped number is wrong: rent per head-month = rentPerAum / auPerHead = $20 (calc.mjs:71); extension practice (and the tool's own totals) price a 1.2-AU pair at $24 x 1.2 = $28.80 a month. Internal check: 71.79 head x 5.92 months x $20 = $8,501, not the $12,243 annual rent the tool shows next to it. The browser status line also states a false range when no deal exists ("rent between $380 and $100 per AUM works for both"), and a blank acres field silently computes 320 acres.
evidence.completeness: Walked every README/page feature in Chromium (Playwright over a local server, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/01267756-bf5d-5ffa-b429-738a5f63cbd7/scratchpad/gl/pw.cjs): Load an example -> 10-row result table (AUMs 510, head 72, rent per AUM/head-month/acre, annual rent $12,243, hay $103, ceiling $100, floor $21), drought table 100/75/50% (510/383/255 AUMs, 72/54/36 head, $12,243/$9,182/$6,121), usage counter {example_loaded:1} in localStorage, no console errors. CLI with the README command prints the same and exits 0; --alt 300 exits 1 with 'No rent works'; CSV builder runs in tests. All claimed features present; rent per head-month present but wrong (scored under correctness). No stubs or TODOs.
evidence.verification: cd ventures/grazing-lease-rate-calculator && node --test '*.test.mjs': 23 tests, 23 pass, 0.29 s. Five mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 2 caught (AUM days 30.4 -> 30; rancher ceiling without the extra cost), 3 survived: rent per head-month / -> * (no test checks that output at all, which is how the inverted formula shipped), the utilisation warning threshold 50 -> 65, and the rancher saving branch inverted (> 0 -> < 0). Tests check AUMs, hay and break-evens; head-month rent, the advice branches and the page status line are untested.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (89 lines), cli.mjs, index.html script, usage.mjs and the three test files. Pure functions, no dependencies, escaped HTML, labelled inputs, guarded local-only usage counter. Defects: analyze() replaces any blank field with a DEFAULTS value (calc.mjs:26), so clearing acres in the page silently computes 320 acres; droughtTable merges DEFAULTS differently (calc.mjs:77), so a blank forage field gives a main result at 2,000 lb and an empty drought table; non-numeric values report camelCase keys ('rentPerAum cannot be negative.' for --rent abc); misnamed variable hayLbsAsFedPerAumDry (it is dry matter); dense money() one-liner.
evidence.claims: Backed: no-warranty and not-advice footer (index.html footer, page.test.mjs), 'nothing is uploaded' (no fetch/XHR/beacon, asserted in page.test.mjs), local-only usage events described accurately, formulas in 'How the numbers work' match calc.mjs, the not-modelled list is honest, served-copy.mjs reports no stale origin in llms.txt/sitemap/robots/canonicals (the github.io link in source llms.txt is rewritten at deploy, source-only). Not backed: 'rent per ... head-month' (README, page, llms.txt) is the inverse of what a head-month costs; the status line asserts a range 'works for both' even when the owner floor exceeds the rancher ceiling (index.html:159); the FAQ says an AUM is 'about 780 lb of dry matter' while the code uses 26 x 30.4 = 790.4 lb.
evidence.fitness: Job walked: a landowner and a rancher agreeing a summer lease for cow-calf pairs. The AUM count, hay ceiling and owner floor are usable for an early range. But pair leases are commonly quoted per pair per month, and that line is 31% low ($20 vs $28.80), so a landowner quoting from it under-prices by about $3,700 a season on the sample; a rancher who types 50% because of 'take half, leave half' gets 103 head where a 25% harvest-efficiency stocking rate gives 51, with no warning. Useful as a calculator only after a user rechecks those two lines.
evidence.domain: Compared with NRCS NRPH ch. 6 (AU, AUM, animal-unit equivalents) and extension stocking-rate guidance (e.g. University of Nebraska and Iowa State pasture rent and stocking-rate publications: harvest efficiency about 25% of total production under continuous grazing, rent per pair = AUM rate x AUE). Sound: AUM from DM intake, hay converted via DM% and waste, owner floor per acre over AUMs/acre. Departures: head-month rent divides by AUE instead of multiplying; 'Share you can graze' is ambiguous between utilisation (50% 'take half') and harvest efficiency (~25%), and the only warning fires above 50%, so the common confusion doubles the stocking rate silently; property tax charged only against the lease side of the owner comparison; no calf-weight or season-adjusted AUE.

defects.what: Rent per head-month divides the AUM rate by animal units per head: a 1.2-AU cow-calf pair at $24/AUM shows $20 a month instead of $28.80 (AUM rate x AUE); the line contradicts the tool's own annual rent (71.79 head x 5.92 months x $20 = $8,501 vs $12,243). Shown in the result table, CSV and claimed in README/llms.txt.
When the owner floor exceeds the rancher ceiling the page status line still says 'rent between $380 and $100 per AUM works for both'.
A blank field silently takes the DEFAULTS value: clearing acres computes 320 acres (255 AUMs, 36 head) with no error; a blank forage field gives a 2,000 lb main result and an empty drought table.

'Share you can graze' is ambiguous between utilisation (50%, 'take half leave half') and harvest efficiency (NRCS/UNL about 25%); the only warning fires above 50%, so the common confusion doubles head carried (102.6 vs 51.3 on the sample) silently.
Three of five seeded mutants survive: rent per head-month is never asserted (how the inverted formula shipped), and the utilisation-warning threshold and rancher-saving branch are untested.
The FAQ says an AUM is 'about 780 lb of dry matter' while the code uses 26 lb x 30.4 days = 790.4 lb.
Non-numeric numeric inputs report the internal key ('rentPerAum cannot be negative.') rather than a plain message.
Owner comparison charges property tax only against the lease (it is owed under the alternative too); no calf-age or season-adjusted animal-unit equivalent.

verdict: A compact, honest AUM lease calculator whose core arithmetic is right: AUMs 510.12, head 71.79, hay $102.72/AUM, rancher ceiling $99.72, owner floor $21.33 and annual rent $12,243 all match a hand build-up from the NRCS AUM definition, and the page and CLI work with the disclaimer and local-only counting they describe. It does not meet the bar. Rent per head-month is inverted ($20 instead of $28.80 for a 1.2-AU pair, calc.mjs:71) and no test looks at it; the status line claims a working range when none exists; blank fields silently become example defaults; and the utilisation input invites a 2x overstocking with no warning. Fixing calc.mjs:71 (multiply), branching the status line on dealExists, rejecting blank required fields and testing those outputs would lift correctness, claims and verification to 3.
